items.followUp: What is the purpose of the <ol> tag in HTML?

rubric.why: Checks that the student identifies the purpose of the UL tag.
rubric.description: States that UL creates an unordered or bulleted list.

rubric.why: Checks that the student identifies how individual entries are marked up.
rubric.description: States that each list item is enclosed in an LI tag.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying LI as the list-item tag.

modelAnswer: The <UL> tag creates an unordered (bulleted) list in HTML.
Each item in the list is written inside an <LI> tag.

items.followUp: Define star and ring topologies, and sketch both.

rubric.why: Checks that the student gives the defining feature of bus topology.
rubric.description: Defines bus topology as computers connected to a common backbone cable.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the shared backbone.

rubric.why: Checks that the student gives the defining feature of mesh topology.
rubric.description: Defines a full mesh as computers directly interconnected with one another.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the direct interconnections.

rubric.why: Checks that the bus sketch includes several computers attached to the common cable.
rubric.description: Draws a recognisable bus diagram with computers branching from a backbone.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a labelled bus sketch showing the shared cable and connected computers.

rubric.why: Checks that the mesh sketch shows a direct link between every pair of computers.
rubric.description: Draws a recognisable full-mesh diagram with all three direct links.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a labelled mesh sketch showing every pair connected.

modelAnswer: Bus topology: All computers are connected to one common backbone cable.
Mesh topology: In a full mesh, each computer is connected directly to the other computers.
